title: Behaviours: “more funds is safer” and friends
objectives: Answer five client behaviours with the manual's “what to say” line.
Explain why scheme assets are safe regardless of AMC count.
body_md:
Many clients believe each extra fund adds safety. Often it only adds paperwork. Diversification myth: “Twelve funds must be safer than four.” Say: “Let's look at what they hold. Most own the same top stocks, so it's really one portfolio.” Fund collecting: “This one was top-rated, so I added it.” Say: “Before adding, let's see what it does that your current funds don't.” Fear of missing out: “What if the fund I drop does best?” Say: “If they hold the same stocks, they'll move together. You won't miss much.” Loyalty: “I've had this fund for years.” Say: “We can keep the old units and just stop new money into it.” Spreading across AMCs: “I use different fund houses to be safe.” Say: “A scheme's assets are held by a trust and custodian, separate from the AMC. What matters is what the funds own.”

| Behaviour | What it sounds like | What to say |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Diversification myth | “Twelve funds must be safer than four.” | “Let's look at what they hold. Most own the same top stocks, so it's really one portfolio.” |
| Fund collecting | “This one was top-rated, so I added it.” | “Before adding, let's see what it does that your current funds don't.” |
| Fear of missing out | “What if the fund I drop does best?” | “If they hold the same stocks, they'll move together. You won't miss much.” |
| Loyalty | “I've had this fund for years.” | “We can keep the old units and just stop new money into it.” |
| Spreading across AMCs | “I use different fund houses to be safe.” | “A scheme's assets are held by a trust and custodian, separate from the AMC. What matters is what the funds own.” |

> **Investor takeaway:** The one line to remember: diversify by what you own, not by how many funds you own.
example: “I use different fund houses to be safe”: scheme assets sit with a trust and custodian, separate from the AMC — what matters is what the funds own.
say: Most own the same top stocks, so it's really one portfolio.
We can keep old units and just stop new money into it.
never: Dropping an overlapping fund means missing its gains.

check.q: “Different AMCs are safer” is answered by…
o: “Scheme assets sit with a trust and custodian; what matters is what funds own”
check.why: “Scheme assets sit with a trust and custodian; what matters is what funds own”. Diversify holdings, not fund houses.

check.q: Should a fund be added once it is top-rated, without checking overlap?
o: No — always check what it adds to existing holdings
Only if it is a small-cap fund
check.why: Always check what it adds to existing holdings.

check.q: “Twelve funds must be safer than four” is:
check.why: Diversification myth: “Twelve funds must be safer than four.” Say: “Let's look at what they hold.”
